About this document

This document provides the teaching content for Visual Arts – Printmaking and
Sculpture Years 12–13 of the New Zealand Curriculum.

Progress and assessment information for Visual Arts – Printmaking and Sculpture
Years 12–13 is still in development. Once that is completed, Visual Arts – Printmaking
and Sculpture Years 12–13 is proposed to be made by the Minister of Education as a
National Curriculum Statement under section 90(1)(a) of the Education and Training
Act 2020.

It is proposed that, once made and published in the New Zealand Gazette, schools
who offer Visual Arts – Printmaking and Sculpture Years 12–13 will be required to
start using it in Year 12 from 1 January 2029, and in Year 13 from 1 January 2030.

This document will be replaced with the official version made under the Act and
published in the New Zealand Gazette once that has occurred.




Visual Arts – Printmaking and Sculpture | Years 12–13 | October 2026                     Page 2

Purpose statement
                                                                      Te toi whakairo, ka ihiihi, ka wehiwehi, ka aweawe
                                                                                                                           Artistic excellence makes the world sit up in wonder.
                                                                      te ao katoa.




  In Visual Arts – Printmaking and Sculpture, students are taught how ideas can be
  developed and communicated through specialised art-making processes,
  materials, and visual language. Building on prior learning in the visual arts,
  students investigate and apply printmaking or sculpture practices to create
  artworks that respond to a central proposition through sustained creative
  investigation.


Students are taught discipline-specific concepts, processes, and conventions, and
how to select and use materials, tools, and techniques with increasing control and
intention. Through 2D or 3D modes of practice, students develop visual language and
technical capability to communicate ideas effectively within their chosen discipline.

Printmaking and Sculpture provides students with the knowledge and practices to
investigate, analyse, evaluate, and apply understanding through sustained art-
making. Students engage with cultural, social, historical, and contemporary contexts,
examining how materials, processes, and artistic conventions shape meaning and
influence interpretation.

As students progress through Years 12 and 13, they are taught to generate, refine,
and present a coherent body of work informed by established practice and their own
creative development. Through experimentation, reflection, and critical decision-
making, students develop increasingly sustained studio practice, artistic agency, and
critical judgement, enabling them to communicate ideas through resolved printmaking
or sculptural works.

  Visual Arts – Printmaking and Sculpture leads to pathways in creative and
  cultural industries, including fine arts, public art, fabrication, creative technologies,
  arts education, and gallery and museum practice.

 Disciplinary writing

 Focus: The use of writing to reflect the ways in which knowledge is organised, analysed, and communicated within the discipline.
 In Visual Arts – Printmaking and Sculpture, students use explicitly taught disciplinary writing to analyse established practice and communicate the creative ideas, processes, intentions, and meanings
 in own and others’ artwork.

 Responsible use of artificial intelligence
 Artificial intelligence (AI) can support learning, research, inquiry, and creative processes, but it may also introduce bias, inaccuracies, ethical concerns, and issues relating to
 ownership. AI should enhance, not replace, critical or creative thinking, source evaluation, subject knowledge, or students’ own analysis and decision-making. Responsible AI use
 emphasises the importance of exercising independent judgement, drawing on credible sources, verifying information, being transparent about AI use, considering diverse
 perspectives, and developing independent thinking.
